# Martin Luk — guest post, his own words (byte-copied sentences)

Source: https://tradingresourcehub.substack.com/p/martin-luk-283-usic-2024-key-lessons
Title: Martin Luk: +283% USIC 2024 key lessons — a guest post written by Martin Luk, edited by Kyna Kosling (The Trading Resource Hub)
Published: 2025-02-01
Fetched: 2026-11-01 (the sentences below, verbatim, curly quotes as published)

## Universe
I mainly trade stocks with >5% ADR for this reason (as illustrated by most trades above), but this isn’t a hard rule.
Focus on high ADR stocks in the hot sector/theme
I spend around 30 minutes a day scanning for the previous day’s high performers (‘potent scan’)
and pre-market gap-ups (‘pre-market scan’).
On weekends, I also scan for the biggest movers of the past 30 days (‘leader scan’).

## Watchlists
Lead: 9 EMA > 21 EMA > 50 EMA.
Mediocre: 9 EMA > 21 EMA < 50 EMA or 9 EMA < 21 EMA > 50 EMA.
Lag: 9 EMA < 21 EMA < 50 EMA.
One for small caps (<$5B market cap); and

## Stops
As I become more experienced, I tightened my stops to 1–5% (mostly)
avoided exceeding half of the stock’s average daily range (ADR)
no more than a 2.5% stop for a 5% ADR stock, etc.
Over 80% of my trades in 2024 used stops of <3.5%.
I define my stop before entering a trade, and place a hard stop as soon as I’m filled

## Risk and size
And I keep account risk at 0.5–1% per trade.
I currently don’t face problems with that, except when trading stocks below $5, for which I reduce my position size.

## Exits
I didn’t follow my 9 EMA trailing stop sell rule and got punished for it.

## His stats
Last year’s win rate was 25%, and I suffered several losing streaks of 10 trades or more.
I also experienced the longest losing streak of my trading career: 18 consecutive losers.
Then, in June–August 2024, I suffered a 30% drawdown.
